Weddings, proposals, engagements, milestones and corporate

Find event planners, wedding planners and party planners across Australia

You should not have to run your own celebration. Tell us what you are planning and how much help you want, and we pass your enquiry to event planners and coordinators who cover your area and work on your kind of event.

The event
The planner

Beautiful events are coordinated, not lucky

Start here

Tell us what you are planning

Two minutes, and nothing here is locked in. You can change any of it when you speak to a planner.

  • 01Four short steps Your event, where and when, how much help you want, then your details.
  • 02Written once One enquiry reaches planners who cover your area and work on your kind of event.
  • 03No cost, no commitment Enquiring is free and you are not committed to booking anyone.

Free enquiry

Tell us what you are planning

Four short steps. Nothing is committed, and the details help a planner tell you quickly whether they can help.

How much help do you want?
Before you send this. Plan Your Event works with My Event Match to process your enquiry and pass it to event planners and coordinators who cover your area. Submitting this form sends the details above through My Event Match so suitable planners can review your request and reply to you directly. Read how we handle your details in our privacy policy.

Sending an enquiry does not commit you to booking anyone. It is free, you choose whether to go ahead, and you pay your planner directly.

How much help?

How much of this do you actually want to hand over?

Most people do not need a planner for everything. Australian planners package their work at three levels, and the level you choose is the single biggest thing that moves the price.

Full event planning

You hand over the whole thing. Your planner builds the concept, finds the venue, books every supplier, holds the budget and runs the day. You approve decisions rather than chase them.

Best when you are time poor, planning from another city, or the guest list is over 100.

  • Concept, styling direction and mood
  • Venue shortlisting and site visits
  • Supplier sourcing, quoting and booking
  • Budget tracking from first deposit to final invoice
  • Run sheet and full day management

Partial planning

You have booked the venue and you have opinions. Your planner picks up everything you have not sorted, which is usually the suppliers, the timeline and the jobs that keep sliding down the list.

Best when the venue and date are locked in but the middle of the plan has stalled.

  • You keep the decisions you care about
  • Supplier shortlists and introductions
  • Timeline and budget management
  • Styling refinement against what is booked
  • Coordination on the day

On-the-day coordination

You plan it. Someone else runs it. Your coordinator takes over your plan around four to six weeks out, confirms every supplier, and becomes the person everyone rings so that nobody rings you.

Best when the planning is done and you simply do not want to be the contact on the day.

  • Your plan and your suppliers stay as they are
  • Handover four to six weeks before
  • Supplier confirmation and briefing
  • Run sheet written and circulated
  • On-site management from bump in to bump out

Compare all planning services

Find a planner

Which kind of planner do you need?

The job titles are not interchangeable. A planner builds the plan, a coordinator runs it, and a party planner works to a different rhythm again. Start with the one that matches your event.

01

Event Planners

The generalists. An event planner takes an occasion of any kind, from a 40th to a product launch, and turns a date and a budget into a plan with suppliers attached to it.

Find event planners
02

Wedding Planners

Wedding work has its own vocabulary, its own supplier network and a twelve to eighteen month lead time. A wedding planner has run the day before, not just events in general.

Find wedding planners
03

Party Planners

Birthdays, milestones, engagements and kids parties. A party planner works to shorter lead times and smaller budgets, and often brings the entertainment and hire relationships with them.

Find party planners
04

Wedding Coordinators

A wedding coordinator steps in near the end. They take the plan you have already built, confirm it, and manage the day itself so the couple is not directing traffic.

Find wedding coordinators
05

Event Coordinators

Coordination for everything that is not a wedding. Logistics, supplier confirmation, run sheets and on-site management for parties, functions and corporate events.

Find event coordinators
06

Venue Sourcing

Sometimes the only thing standing between you and a plan is a room. Venue sourcing is a standalone service where a planner shortlists and negotiates on your behalf.

About venue sourcing

By occasion

What are you planning?

Every occasion has its own pressure points. Tell us which one you are working on and the enquiry goes to planners who have run that kind of event before.

Weddings

The longest lead time and the most suppliers of anything on this list. Australian couples typically start looking for planning help nine to fourteen months out.

Wedding planning

Proposals

A proposal is a short, high stakes event that has to stay secret. Proposal planners handle the location, the styling, the photographer and the timing without the other person knowing.

Proposal planning

Engagement Parties

The first party after the yes. Usually 40 to 80 guests, planned in three to four months, and often the first time a couple works with a planner at all.

Engagement party planning

Corporate Events

Conferences, awards nights, launches and staff celebrations, where the brief comes with a budget approval process and a run sheet other people need to sign off.

Corporate event planning

See every occasion we cover

Why a planner

What does hiring a planner actually get you?

It gets you out of the middle. Planning an event is mostly a coordination job, and the person doing it ends up as the switchboard for everyone else. The supplier who has not replied in nine days. The budget spreadsheet that stopped adding up in March. The run sheet nobody else has read. The three group chats you are the admin of.

A planner takes the switchboard. They already know which caterers work with a dry hire venue, what a realistic bump in window looks like, and which questions to ask a venue before you sign. That knowledge is the actual product. The styling is the visible part.

What a planner does not do is take the event away from you. A good one makes your decisions happen faster. If a planner is telling you what your event should look like rather than asking, that is the wrong planner, and you should keep talking to the others.

You keep the decisions

A planner's job is to execute your brief and tell you honestly when something will not work, not to replace your taste with theirs.

They arrive with a supplier list

Most of the value in the first month is the shortlist. A working planner already knows who is reliable in your city and who is not taking bookings.

They own the timeline

The run sheet is the deliverable that matters on the day. It is also the thing almost nobody produces properly when they plan alone.

How it works

Four steps, and you stop carrying it

01

Tell us what you are planning

The occasion, roughly when, the suburb or postcode, and how much help you want. It takes about two minutes and you do not need the details finalised.

02

We pass it to relevant planners

Your enquiry goes to event planners and coordinators who cover your area and work on your kind of event, through My Event Match.

03

Compare what comes back

Planners reply to you directly with their pricing, what is included at your level, and how they would approach the event.

04

Choose and hand it over

You engage the planner you want and pay them directly. There is no cost to enquire and no obligation to book any of them.

Straight answers

Event planning questions, answered

What does an event planner do?

An event planner builds and runs the plan behind an event. That covers the concept, the venue, the supplier shortlist, the quotes, the contracts, the budget, the timeline and the management of the day itself. How much of that list your planner takes depends on whether you book full planning, partial planning or on-the-day coordination.

How much does a planner cost in Australia?

Published Australian ranges vary widely. Easy Weddings, in a guide updated in February 2026, puts a day-of coordinator at roughly $1,500 to $2,000 and full-service planning at $5,000 to $6,000. Airtasker's Australian cost guide gives a wider $1,000 to $20,000 spread with a median around $8,000, and notes that many planners charge 10 to 15 per cent of the total budget instead of a flat fee. The gap between those two sets of numbers is mostly scope. Our planner cost guide breaks it down properly.

Is it free to enquire?

Yes. Sending an enquiry through Plan Your Event costs nothing and does not commit you to booking anyone. If you go ahead with a planner, you engage and pay that planner directly.

How quickly will I hear back?

Planners reply to you directly, so the timing depends on the individual planner and how busy the season is. Spring and autumn are the peak wedding months in most of Australia and replies can take longer then. If you have a firm date coming up, say so in your enquiry.

Who receives my enquiry?

Plan Your Event works with My Event Match to process enquiries and pass them to event planners and coordinators who cover your area and work on your kind of event. The details you submit are sent through My Event Match so those planners can review your request and reply to you. Our privacy policy sets out how your information is handled.

How far ahead should I book a planner?

For a wedding, most Australian couples engage a planner nine to fourteen months out, and on-the-day coordinators are usually booked two to three months out. Milestone parties and corporate events generally run on a three to six month lead time. Enquiring earlier costs nothing and gives you more planners to choose from.

Do you plan the event yourselves?

No. Plan Your Event is not a planning company. We are a discovery and enquiry service that connects people planning weddings, parties and private celebrations with independent event planners and coordinators around Australia.

One enquiry, then it is somebody else's job

Meaningful celebrations. Beautifully planned.

Tell us what you are planning and we will pass it to planners who work on your kind of event.

Free to enquire. No obligation to book. You pay your planner directly.
